extracted.subtask_description: A wire-service compilation of international news dispatches (UN/Suez Canal, Saar, Cyprus, Poland, etc.), reporting events, official statements, and operational facts from multiple locations. Focus is on diplomatic, military, and maritime developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstention from repeated threats
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed by U.N. Secretary-General Dag Hammarskjold as one recommended unilateral move to improve the Palestine situation; presented as a behavioral standard for governments/parties to reduce tensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for demilitarized zones
rubrics_metrics.description: "Respect for demilitarized zones set up in the 1949 armistice agreement."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hammarskjold cites strict respect for existing demilitarized zones as a concrete unilateral measure to help stabilize the situation; implies enforcement of armistice boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom for Israeli navigation in the Suez Canal
rubrics_metrics.description: "Freedom for Israeli navigation in the Suez Canal as called for by a council resolution of Sept. 1, 1951."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of Hammarskjold's suggested unilateral moves; references an existing Security Council resolution and frames freedom of navigation as a legal/political standard to reduce friction (Egyptian objections noted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict adherence to the cease-fire
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named by Hammarskjold as a necessary unilateral practice to prevent incidents that could undermine the cease-fire and law; emphasized as a high-level compliance requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repatriation and resettlement of Palestine-war refugees
rubrics_metrics.description: "Repatriation and resettlement of almost a million Arab Palestine-war refugees now living largely on relief in Arab countries bordering Israel."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a major humanitarian/political measure to address root causes of instability; cited by Hammarskjold as part of steps to improve conditions in the region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utilization of Jordan waters (water-sharing)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Utilization of Jordan waters," for which water-sharing plans are still pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hammarskjold lists equitable utilization of water resources (Jordan waters) as a pending technical/political measure necessary for regional stability; implies negotiation and implementation of water-sharing plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governments must exert firm discipline on their forces
rubrics_metrics.description: Hammarskjold declared the governments concerned had failed to exert on their forces "a discipline sufficiently firm to forestall incidents which, step by step, must necessarily undermine the cease-fire."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames an expectation/standard of state responsibility: authorities should control and discipline military/police forces to prevent violations and escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convoy speed limits for Suez transit
rubrics_metrics.description: For the approach: maximum speed of 8 knots; top speed in the canal is 7 1/2 knots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational navigation rule cited in the on-the-scene report to maintain safe convoy spacing and control in the narrow canal; used to manage convoy flow and collision risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing between ships in convoy (ballast vs loaded)
rubrics_metrics.description: The distance between ships (in ballast--without cargo) should not exceed 1,350 yards, or approximately five minutes sailing time; loaded ships go through at longer intervals since they take more time to stop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety standard for convoy intervals to allow stopping distance in an emergency; differentiates requirements depending on loading condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping distances for empty and loaded ships
rubrics_metrics.description: An empty ship can be stopped by backing engines in about 600 yards; loaded ships require longer stopping distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical navigational constraint cited by an experienced pilot; explains why spacing/interval rules differ and why convoy pacing is conservative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supertanker momentum and halt time
rubrics_metrics.description: Supertankers over 30,000 tons require 10 to 15 minutes to halt; some big tankers, when loaded, go six miles on momentum alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights extreme momentum and braking limitations of large vessels, underscoring the need for long intervals and careful convoy management in confined waterways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot duties and interval management between stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Pilots check company stations between Port Said and Suez to find out the interval between convoys; pilots are on the bridge constantly except when their convoy gets a little space as another convoy passes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes procedural practices for pilots managing convoy timing and handoffs; a standard operational routine to coordinate safe passage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigational channel constraints (width and depth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Main channel marked by buoys is 180 to 240 feet wide; the main channel is 42 feet deep and big ships sometimes have only four feet of water under their hulls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical constraints that set implicit safety/operational standards: narrow width and shallow margins limit maneuverability and require strict convoy discipline and speed/spacing rules.
